title: SharePoint forms: Power Automate trigger "When a form is submitted" and action "Get form metadata"
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, data policy navigation, PowerShell call and policy administration roles match the sources checked. It distinguishes the documented connector and form-creation requirements from the unpublished operation-specific licensing and rollout details.

claims.claim: The update introduces the When a form is submitted trigger and Get form metadata action for forms in SharePoint.
claims.quote:
With this update, a new trigger and action are now available in Power Automate:
Trigger: When a form is submitted

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Submitting a list form, file upload form or document generation form triggers a flow rather than requiring someone to start the flow manually.
claims.quote: Use this trigger to start a Power Automate flow when a supported form in SharePoint receives a response. Supported form types include list forms, file upload forms, and document generation forms.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Makers can build downstream approvals, notifications or routing based on submitted responses.
claims.quote: This enables automation of downstream processes such as approvals, notifications, routing, or document workflows based on submitted responses.

claims.claim: Get form metadata returns the form identifier, title, link, form type, output format and questions so a flow can inspect its schema.
claims.quote: The returned metadata includes information such as the form identifier, title, link, form type, defined output format, and the questions used to collect responses.

claims.claim: The trigger provides the form ID.
claims.quote: The trigger provides submission-level details, including the form ID, responder information, submission time, and responses to form questions.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The default state and whether the operations appear for all makers at once are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint forms Power Automate trigger action tenant admin switch rollout existing flows; SharePoint form Power Automate rollout default. Opened the roadmap, connector article, SharePoint reference and document generation page; no arrival default or distribution found.

claims.claim: The roadmap and checked Learn documentation describe no change to existing forms or flows or to users who build no flow.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint forms Power Automate trigger action tenant admin switch rollout existing flows. Opened the roadmap, connector article, SharePoint reference and document generation page; none specifies changes to existing forms or flows.

claims.claim: No feature-specific administrator action or admin-center switch limiting these operations is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint When a form is submitted enable disable admin. Opened the roadmap, connector article, SharePoint reference and data policy pages; no operation-specific switch or required admin action found.

claims.claim: The Business classification is reached in Power Platform admin center through Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Prebuilt connectors > SharePoint > Move to Business.
claims.quote:
In the Security pane, under Settings, select Data and privacy.
select the Data policy section.
select a policy, and then select Edit Policy.
Select the Prebuilt connectors step
select the Salesforce and SharePoint connectors, and then select Move to Business

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy GUID> -Classification Confidential -Connectors <connector objects> moves the specified connectors into the policy's Business group.
claims.quote:
Add-ConnectorsToPolicy
    [-PolicyName] <String>
    [-Classification] <String>
    [-Connectors] <Object[]>
Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.where: controls[0].governs; summary; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing data policies govern which connectors flows in the scoped environments may combine with SharePoint.
claims.quote: By moving the Salesforce and SharePoint connectors to the Business data group, you're preventing users from creating flows and apps that combine these two connectors with any of the connectors in the Non-business or Blocked groups.

claims.claim: SharePoint is not blockable, so its Block action is unavailable.
claims.quote: For connectors like SharePoint that aren't blockable, the Block action isn't available and a warning appears.

claims.claim: Connector action control allows or blocks individual connector actions and triggers.
claims.quote: You can use connector action control to allow or block individual actions or triggers within a given connector.

claims.claim: Connector action control is documented for blockable connectors, not unblockable connectors, so the described data policy control does not individually disable these SharePoint operations.
claims.quote: You can configure connector actions for all blockable connectors, but not for unblockable connectors and custom connectors.

claims.claim: The tenant-level policy procedure requires the Power Platform Administrator role.
claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: The environment-level policy procedure requires Environment Admin permissions outside environments with a Dataverse database.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions.

claims.claim: For an environment with a Dataverse database, the environment-level policy procedure instead requires the System Administrator role.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: Environment admins cannot edit policies created by the tenant admin.
claims.quote: Environment admins can't edit policies created by the tenant admin.

claims.claim: Environment-level data policies cannot override tenant-wide data policies.
claims.quote: Environment-level data policies can't override tenant-wide data policies.

claims.claim: Learn says document generation form submitters need only the form link.
claims.quote: Form submitters need only the form link (Read access to the template is granted automatically).

claims.claim: Creating a document generation form requires Edit permission on the document library.
claims.quote: To create a form, users must have Edit permissions on the document library.

claims.quote: Content managers, or users who create and configure forms, must have a Microsoft Copilot license assigned.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: No separate licensing requirement or rate specific to the submission trigger and metadata action was found.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint Get form metadata pricing license meter. Opened the SharePoint connector reference, connector article, licensing/types and document generation page; no separate license or rate for either operation found.

claims.claim: The cited licensing page does not itemize these operations, and the connector article names no separate meter or price for them.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint Get form metadata pricing license meter. Read licensing/types and the SharePoint connector article, including the form trigger and metadata sections; neither gives an operation-specific charge or individual licensing coverage.

claims.claim: The document generation page states the Copilot license requirement for creating and configuring forms, without tying it to running the two flow operations.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint Get form metadata license price permissions. Read the document generation page's Prerequisites and Use Power Automate sections; the license is assigned to users creating and configuring forms, with no separate flow-operation requirement stated.

claims.claim: The connector article does not state the permissions a flow owner needs to use these operations on another person's form.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint When a form is submitted permissions connection; SharePoint Get form metadata license price permissions. Read the connector article and SharePoint reference form-operation parameters; no permission rule for using someone else's form was stated.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects the Standard connector entitlement and the separately assigned Copilot license required for document generation form creation.
claims.quote: Content managers, or users who create and configure forms, must have a Microsoft Copilot license assigned.

claims.claim: Power Automate does not apply form conditional visibility, so a required field hidden in the form remains visible in a document generated through a flow.
claims.quote: Power Automate doesn't apply conditional visibility: if you generate documents through a Power Automate flow, the flow doesn't hide or show fields the way the form does, so a required field that your form hides will still be visible in the document.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises making fields normally hidden by the form optional when using the form with Power Automate.
claims.quote: When you use a form with Power Automate, make any field you'd normally hide an optional field so it doesn't block the intended flow.
